quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 44

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are already in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the road mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What is a good way to prevent fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and rest or sleep.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They will run into the street without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will run into the street without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The lane with the least traffic.

questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the left lane, which is closest to the lane you came from.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Why does night driving require more caution?

options.text: There are more vehicles on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as clearly. You must use your headlights from one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells drivers that a new lane will be added to the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers in the left lane that they must turn left.

questions.question: When you see a red traffic light, you should:

options.text: Drive through if no cars are coming.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is watching.

questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red if no sign says otherwise.

questions.question: When driving on highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Avoid looking at one spot for more than a few seconds to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross quickly as fast as possible.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat the train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially without lights or gates. Make sure your entire vehicle can fit on the other side before crossing. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when you see:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
A traffic officer telling you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, red lights (flashing or steady), and when a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bikers, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These activities take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Distracted drivers have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells you which direction traffic flows on a one-way street. You must drive in the direction shown.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: You see a driver ahead using one hand and talking to a passenger. You should:

options.text: Know that driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers or other things while driving. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. Go to the next turn or exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: What should you do to prepare for hazards ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and both sides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Scan the entire road ahead, including both sides. Find and identify problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: If an oncoming car has bright headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: What is the correct order for changing lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal first, then check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as fast as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, first yield to any traffic and pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is coming. Enter at low speed and yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulation sign is posted at traffic lights where turning right on red is not allowed. You must obey this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead curves only to the right.
The road ahead turns sharply to the right.
The road ahead curves right, then left.
The road ahead curves left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road curves right and then left.

questions.question: What do these signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Warning signs prepare drivers for upcoming road conditions. They are usually yellow with black markings. These object markers warn drivers about hazardous objects or areas to avoid.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
You are entering a school parking lot.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers a school zone is ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Follow what other drivers are doing, even if it goes against the guard's instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow normal driving rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Obey signs, crossing guards, and police officers directing traffic. Always use extra caution in school zones.

questions.question: What is this sign used to warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane ends ahead. Traffic in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to your previous direction of travel.

questions.question: You notice a vehicle defect that may affect safe operation. What should you do?

options.text: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
Fix the defect when you have money.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fix the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Any defect that may affect safe operation should be fixed immediately. Do not drive the vehicle until it is repaired.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They mark where drivers must stop.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
The maximum safe speed under all road conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the maximum legal speed for that road under good conditions. When conditions are poor, you should drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road turns sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you about an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready to stop for a red light, slow down for a yellow light, or watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and drive through.
Stop, look all directions, then proceed.
Be ready to yield if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid crashes. Release the gas pedal, keep your foot near the brake, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: When driving past a car that just parked on the roadside, what should you do?

options.text: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the driver to open the door as you pass.
questions.explanation: When passing a vehicle that just parked, be ready for the driver to open the door. Always drive carefully near parked cars.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic that moves in opposite directions.

questions.question: A driver's left arm is extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points up, they are signaling a right turn. Watch for this hand signal and adjust your driving.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean no passing or lane changes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield first.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield to emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens. Give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Is texting while driving legal?

options.text: Yes, it is legal but not recommended.
Yes, but only for experienced drivers.

questions.explanation: In Indiana, you cannot type, send, or read text messages or emails while driving. The only exception is to contact emergency services.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn. What should you do?

options.text: Signal with your wheels turned left.
Flash your headlights to ask other drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.
